senses.gloss: cut and polished stone block, used for paving floors, stone pavement, mosaic.
units: <cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 28:10">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXVIII</cite> <he>אבן פסי׳ שיש וכ׳</he> ed. Schechter (ed. <he>פיספס</he>) a paving block which has four polished sides (a metaphor for a many-sided scholar).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:32">Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵇ</cite> top <he>בשאין שם פ׳</he> where there is no stone pavement. Ib. XII, beg. 13ᶜ (Chald. dict.) <he>מקטע פ׳</he> he who trims a paving stone (or die, v. infra).

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 10:7">Ex. R. s. 10</cite> <he>בתיהם של גדולים … בשיש בפ׳</he> the houses of the nobles which were paved with marble or blocks; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 102:1">Yalk. Sam. 102</cite> <he>בתי השיש והפִּסְפְּסִים</he> (pl.); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 820:10">Yalk. Ps. 820</cite> <he>בתי השיש ובתי הפ׳</he> (<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 105:10">Midr. Till. to Ps. CV</cite> <he>בתי הסיפים</he>, v. <cite ref="O01308"><he>סַף</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 1:25">Deut. R. s. 1</cite> <he>ואם בפ׳ הפ׳ וכ׳</he> and if (she wipes her hands) on the pavement, the pavement will be blackened, but her hands will not be clean; a. e.—Pl. <he>פְּסִיפְסִים</he>, <he>פְּסִיפְסִין</he>, <he>פִּסְפְּ׳</he>, <cite ref="Q01229"><he>פִּיסְ׳</he></cite>. Yalk. Sam. l. c.; Yalk. Ps. l. c., v. supra.

<cite ref="Mishnah Middot 1:6">Midd. I, 6</cite> <he>ראשי פסי׳ וכ׳</he> Var. in Ar. s. v. <cite ref="Q02091"><he>פשפש</he></cite> (Mish. ed. <he>פספ׳</he>; Talm. ed. <he>פישפשין</he>) the ends of the flag-stones in the pavement indicated the mark between the sacred and the secular grounds; [comment.: blocks on the ceiling]; ib. II, 6; a. e.—[<cite ref="Tosefta Zevahim 7:1">Tosef. Zeb. VII, 1</cite> <he>פסיפסין</he>, Var. <he>פסיפיסין</he>, v. <cite ref="Q02091"><he>פִּשְׁפָשׁ</he> I</cite>.]

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:7:2">Y. R. Hash. I, 57ᶜ</cite> top (expl. <he>המשחק בקוביא</he>) <he>המשחק בפסי׳</he> he who plays with dice; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 25b">Snh. 25ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>בפיספ׳</he> (Rashi: blocks of wood); Y. l. c. <he>משישבור את פְּסִיפְסָיו</he> (he is not reinstated from his civil disabilities,) until he breaks his dice; Snh. l. c. <he>משישברו את פִּיסְפְּסֵיהֶן</he>; Y. Shebu. VII, 37ᵈ bot. <he>פִּיסְפְּסָיו</he>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:5:2">Y. Snh. III, beg., 21ᵃ</cite> (also <cite ref="Q02080"><he>פְּשִׂיפְשִׂין</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 26:8">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXVI, 10</cite> <he>אלי המשחקין בפספ׳ וכ׳</he> that means those who play with dice, who calculate (throw) with the left hand and press with the right hand, and rob and wrong one another; a. e.

<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 11:7">Neg. XI, 7</cite> <he>והרי הוא פסי׳ יחידי</he> ed. Dehr. (ed. <cite ref="Q01345"><he>פספס</he></cite>) suppose there is only one (white) stripe in the whole garment?—Pl. as ab.
<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 11:7">Ib.</cite> <he>קייטא שיש בה פ׳ צבועים וכ׳</he> a pieced sheet in which there are checkers colored and white; Tosef. ib. V, 10.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 927:8">Yalk. Job 927</cite> <he>פספסין הדֵּיהוֹת שלו מכחות וכ׳</he> (or <he>הדּוּחוֹת</he>, not <he>פספסי הרוחות</he>) the faintest checkers (or stripes) of the Leviathan’s skin outshine the sun (v.
Lam. R. to II, 1, v. חִיתּוּךְ.—[The contact between the Hebrew and Greek languages influenced the form פסיפס and the coincidence of some meanings of our word with ψῆφος pebble.]
